rubric.role_summary: Staff-level deep learning compiler engineering for edge AI hardware, focused on compiler optimization, neural network lowering, and performance across the hardware–software boundary.
rubric.search_query:
Find candidates for this role:
Staff-level deep learning compiler engineering for edge AI hardware, focused on compiler optimization, neural network lowering, and performance across the hardware–software boundary.
Mandatory professional qualifications:
- BS, MS, or Ph.D. in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related field.
- 8+ years of hands-on experience developing deep learning compilers or compiler infrastructures; named infrastructures are examples, not a requirement to know all of them.
- Proficiency in C++ and Python.
- Familiarity with modern AI/ML frameworks and deep learning operator representations; the named frameworks are examples, not an all-framework requirement.
- Understanding of computer systems, memory hierarchies, parallel processing, and CPU/GPU/NPU instruction execution.
Preferred, not mandatory:
- Experience with low-level kernel optimization, SIMD/vector programming, and memory allocation strategy development.
- Knowledge of model quantization methodologies and post-training/QAT optimization techniques.
- Prior experience with software stacks for custom AI accelerators, DSPs, or embedded architectures.
- Experience with FPGA bring-up, hardware emulation, or cycle-accurate simulator development.
- Strong proficiency in C++ and Python, with fundamentals in data structures, algorithms, and object-oriented design.
Work location and geographic eligibility:
Accept any one of these geographic alternatives (OR): San Francisco Bay Area, California. Specific cities and metropolitan areas also include any location within about 100 miles (160 km) of them; states, countries, and regions require a location inside them.
